newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares rise on political hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares rise on political hopes.

text.p: Expectations that a solution may be found to a 10-day old political crisis pushed Indian shares higher on Tuesday, brokers said.
"If a mid-term poll is avoided I see the market rebounding strongly," said Mathew Easow, a broker at the Calcutta Stock Exchange (CSE).

The head of India's Congress party, Sitaram Kesri, told Reuters in New Delhi on Tuesday that he was ready to hold talks with the United Front (UF) provided the ruling alliance came forward with a proposal.
"I am ready for talks if the proposal comes from their side. There is no doubt in it," Kesri said.
UF spokesman Jaipal Reddy later told reporters the formal talks will begin on Wednesday.
"It is a very positive development," said Rajesh Bajaj, director at Calcutta brokerage Lohia Securities. "This has given a boost to sagging confidence."
The markets have been in jitters since Kesri plunged the country into a political crisis on March 30 when he pulled his party's crucial support to the minority UF government.

In Bombay kerb deals, SBI was quoted at 273/274 rupees against Monday's closing of 265.75, ITC at 371/372 against 361, Reliance at 269/270 against 264.25 and TISCO at 166/167 against 161.50, traders said.
In Calcutta, ITC rose 10.50 rupees to 374.10, SBI 8.30 to 274.60, ACC 22.0 to 1,316, Hindustan Lever 15.50 to 1,044, Reliance 5.30 to 269.10 and TELCO 6.50 to 370.
"The moving force behind the market tomorrow will be the political developments," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Bombay brokerage Kotak Securities Ltd.
A political resolution would help the passage of a pro-business budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) which is before parliament.
